name: Agents
description: Claude Code and Codex threads in a sidebar laid out like T3 Code's: pinned and active threads on top, snoozed and settled ones below, a project filter. Each thread is a chat: its work folded behind how long it took, questions and plans answered above the box to write in, messages queued or steered while it works, back to any message or forked from any answer, a diff panel beside it, and git per thread with the model writing commit messages, pull requests and branch names. Runs your own claude and codex CLIs on the server's machine; threads stay on that machine.
author: Vaultite

harness.label: New threads use
harness.description: the agent a new thread starts with (each thread can pick its own)

mode.label: Access
mode.description: what a new thread may do without asking: supervised asks before commands and file changes; auto-accept edits asks only before commands; auto lets the agent's own reviewer approve routine actions; full access never asks

followUp.label: Follow-up behavior
followUp.description: a message sent while the agent works waits for the turn to end (queue) or goes into it (steer); ⌘↩ does the other for one message

groupByProject.label: Group threads by project
groupByProject.description: the sidebar as T3 Code's legacy one: threads under each project instead of one list

settleAfterDays.label: Settle after days
settleAfterDays.description: a thread nothing happened in for this many days settles by itself (0: never)

settleOnMerge.label: Settle when merged
settleOnMerge.description: a thread whose pull request is merged settles by itself (a closed one always does)

claudeModel.label: Claude model
claudeModel.description: the model new Claude Code threads use (opus, sonnet, haiku or a full name); Claude Code's default when left out

codexModel.label: Codex model
codexModel.description: the model new Codex threads use, as Codex names it; Codex's default when left out

allowUsers.label: Other tailnet logins
allowUsers.description: tailnet logins besides this machine's owner that may use agents (they run on this machine), like someone@example.com
